articles.body: The second screen of nakodo.app is a mock of a creator's page in the app: charts, a fit panel, a line about where the email address came from. On its own it is a picture, and a picture of a product tells you nothing about which part of it matters. So it explains itself. Once it is on screen, a note opens next to one detail, then moves to the next, five times, and after that each note still opens when you hover the thing it belongs to. Go and scroll to it before reading on, because the first design decision is only visible while you do. The notes are part of the page A tooltip library puts the note in a portal at the end of body and positions it with script against the viewport.

articles.title: Our page polls a 16-character fingerprint, and only a change is allowed to re-render it
articles.excerpt: A campaign in Nakodo is meant to be left alone. It searches, it writes to the contacts it finds, it reads the replies. So the screen you leave open is a screen whose numbers are wrong a minute later,…
articles.body: A campaign in Nakodo is meant to be left alone. It searches, it writes to the contacts it finds, it reads the replies. So the screen you leave open is a screen whose numbers are wrong a minute later, and the honest fix is that the page should fill itself in. router.refresh() on a timer does that. It keeps client state, so filters you set and text you are typing survive. What it does not keep is cheap: the campaign page is several counts, a list of creators and a couple of correlated subqueries, and running all of that every thirty seconds to find out that nothing happened is the whole cost of the feature with none of the benefit. So the page asks a smaller question first.

articles.body: 내 GPU로 참여한다. 양자 하드웨어는 필요 없다. 오픈 퀀텀 챌린지는 벤더 중립, 완전 재현 가능한 양자 컴퓨팅 벤치마크다. 동결된 문제를 받아 자신의 GPU에서 어떤 방법으로든 풀고 예측 파일을 제출한다. 비공개 정답으로 모든 제출을 동일하게 채점하므로 순위는 재현 가능하고 하드웨어에 무관하다. 2개 시즌, 각 상금 $1,000 시즌 1은 양자 시뮬레이션이다. 페르미 허버드 계(체인, 사다리, 플라켓)의 바닥상태 에너지를 보고한다. 엄밀 대각화 대비 평균절대오차로 채점한다. 마감 2027년 2월 28일. 시즌 2는 QEC 디코더다. 동결된 회전 표면코드 데이터(거리 5, p = 0.005, 회로수준 잡음)를 디코딩한다. 논리 오류율로 채점한다. 마감 2027년 3월 31일. 시즌별 상금은 1위 $600, 2위 $300, 3위 $100. 참가 방법 공개 입력을 받는다. 허깅페이스 FINAL-Bench/oqc-data. 내 GPU에서 푼다. 참고 하네스는 github.com/final-bench/quantum-bench-harness. 챌린지 Space에서 허깅페이스로 로그인하고 예측 JSON을 제출한다. 제출은 수 분 내 자동 채점되어 본인 허깅페이스 프로필로 실시간 순위표에 올라온다. 정답은 비공개, 하네스와 동결 문제는 공개, 사다리는 모두에게 동일하다.

articles.title: Open Quantum Challenge (OQC): a reproducible, hardware-free quantum benchmark
articles.excerpt: Run it on your own GPU. No quantum hardware required. The Open Quantum Challenge is a vendor neutral, fully reproducible benchmark for quantum computing methods. You download a frozen problem, solve i…
articles.body: Run it on your own GPU. No quantum hardware required. The Open Quantum Challenge is a vendor neutral, fully reproducible benchmark for quantum computing methods. You download a frozen problem, solve it with any method on your GPU, and submit a prediction file. A private answer key scores every entry the same way, so the ranking is reproducible and independent of hardware. Two seasons, $1,000 prize each Season 1 is Quantum Simulation. Report the ground state energy of Fermi Hubbard systems (chains, ladders, plaquettes). Scored by mean absolute error against exact diagonalization. Deadline 28 February 2027. Season 2 is QEC Decoder. Decode a frozen rotated surface code dataset (distance 5, p = 0.005, circuit level noise). Scored by logical error rate. Deadline 31 March 2027.

articles.title: NASA Demonstrates Next-Generation Heat Shield Technologies
articles.excerpt: NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24th cargo resupply missi…
articles.body: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) A KREPE-3 capsule floats inside the Northrup Grumman Cygnus XL 24 cargo spacecraft on October 7. Inside the capsule is a 3-D printed heat shield designed by researchers at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. NASA NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24 th cargo resupply mission for NASA undocked from the International Space Station, it carried a fleet of 12 small, experimental capsules designed to test the next generation of thermal protection materials that could serve as the foundation for future heat shields.
